name: Tornado Cash Governance executes an unpinned proposal target
summary: Governance.execute(uint256) reads only proposal.target and re-checks Address.isContract(target) before target.delegatecall(executeProposal()). The Proposal struct stores an address and never binds the code that was voted on, so the deployed code cannot tell that the runtime at the approved address changed after the ballot closed. Configuration.sol states the intended invariant in the deployed source itself - VOTING_DELAY is documented as needed 'to prevent reorg attacks that replace the proposal' - but the implemented protection covers only reorgs, not SELFDESTRUCT plus CREATE2 redeployment at the same address. Proposal 20's target 0xc503893b3e3c0c6b909222b45f2a3a259a52752d carried a benign 1513-byte runtime (hash 0xf7caba6622c5dfc3a02619f85f224ed0fff459af31bdeaa586eb04828cd00149) from its creation at block 17249477 through block 17299105, was self-destructed to empty code at block 17299106, and held a different 5079-byte runtime (hash 0x6ae6d1594daf6781285e59fbe5a02e67b868acf133401847ec022a93c2cd3bce) from block 17299107 onwards. Thirty-two blocks later the Governance proxy delegatecalled that substituted runtime, which wrote 100 lockedBalance entries of 10,000e18 and one of 200,000e18 into Governance storage slot 59 - 1,200,000 TORN of voting weight that was never deposited - against roughly 70,000 legitimate votes. The violated invariant is that an executed proposal performs the action token holders approved; the boundary test finds no parameter value that restores it, because EXECUTION_DELAY, VOTING_PERIOD, QUORUM_VOTES and PROPOSAL_THRESHOLD constrain timing and weight, never the identity of the code at the approved address.
notes: The second and last pre-exploit EIP-1967 Upgraded event on the Governance proxy selected the GovernanceStakingUpgrade implementation, which was deployed in the same transaction by the proxy itself while executing an earlier proposal.

The quantity is exact and reconstructed from receipts, not from reporting. Reversing keccak256(abi.encode(address, 59)) over the 102 Governance storage slots written by the anchor transaction identifies 49 of the addresses whose lockedBalance was fabricated; those 49 addresses then withdrew from the TornadoVault 0x2f50508a8a3d323b91336fa3ea6ae50e55f32185 in three transactions (4,000 TORN in 0x65fa5b47, 6,000 TORN in 0xdf9dbfe1 and 473,000 TORN in 0x13e2b735), totalling exactly 483,000.000000000000000000 TORN of other users' locked deposits, all consolidated into 0x092123663804f8801b9b086b03b98d706f77bd59. Marking that quantity at the DefiLlama TORN spot price of USD 6.40 at the anchor timestamp would give USD 3.09 million and is not realisable: 483,000 TORN was roughly a tenth of circulating supply and the attacker's own dumping into thin DEX liquidity realised only 493.24082618920283 ETH (about USD 0.9 million at the ETH price of that day) for roughly 444,727 TORN, leaving 38,302.57 TORN transferred on unsold at block 17329628. The recorded USD figure is therefore the reported one, Halborn's USD 2,173,500 for the 483,000 TORN, which prices the stolen deposits at about USD 4.50, between the attacker's DEX realisation and the pre-incident spot. The 1,646.9 TORN that the anchor transaction moved from the staking contract into Governance is the relayer-penalty action that voters actually approved and is not counted. Nothing was recovered; the attacker later restored governance control but kept the TORN.

The USD total is the reported valuation of an exact TORN quantity. TORN was too illiquid for the stolen 483,000 to be marked at the anchor spot price, and the attacker's realised DEX proceeds cover only part of the quantity, so the figure carries reporting rather than receipt provenance.

The seed inventory classified this row governance-design on the reasoning that the mutated contract sat outside the victim. Review reverses that: the mutated contract is the vehicle, but the failing check is inside the victim's own deployed implementation, which authorises a delegatecall against an address it never binds to the approved code.
